checkpoints.title: Never layer L04 (Quality Architect's floors): the dast floor runs by default for web and api platforms. Why: Decision #485 makes DAST a default floor under guardrails G1-G3. What changes: internal/verify/dast.go runs the pinned ZAP image under Docker or Podman; it runs the active XSS and injection rules only against an app the seed started on loopback, or a URL the protected config opts in (G1); with no runnable target it records `skipped: dast: no runnable target`, which blocks the floors until a floor waiver (G3); a high alert is advisory before verify.new_floors_blocking_from (Decision #480) and fails from it. verify.SecurityFloors() adds DAST, and Run.NoSeed lets `verify --security` scan without running the seed. internal/proof/pack.go: a `skipped: dast:` check blocks ship until a floor waiver, as a skipped mobile floor does. CONSTRAINTS.md is regenerated from defaults.toml. No other floor or threshold changes
contracts: internal/verify/dast.go DAST.Run: n/a off the web and api platforms; HTTPURL refuses a target that is not an absolute http(s) URL before any skip; ContainerRuntime picks docker, then podman; none is a non-blocking skip locally and a failure with --ci

internal/verify/dast.go: active = started (seeded, not up before the seed, loopback) or an active_scan opt-in that the base revision's .aayudha/config.toml already names for the same environment and url (approvedAtBase)

internal/verify/dast.go: docker.io/zaproxy/zap-stable pinned by sha256 digest; --network host on Linux, host.docker.internal or host.containers.internal elsewhere; a nonzero ZAP exit without a report blocks
internal/verify/verify.go: SecurityFloors() = sast, secrets, deps, dast; Run.NoSeed
internal/verify/web.go: the dast target resolves as the web floors resolve theirs and still refuses a production environment
internal/proof/pack.go: SkippedDAST; BlocksShip(check) is true for a skipped dast check whose detail starts `skipped: dast:`
instrumentation: the dast check detail in the proof pack says active or passive, names the runtime and the image digest, and names the fix on a skip
an advisory miss before the blocking date names the date and the alert
checkpoints.rollback: revert the PR, or set [verify] dast = false in .aayudha/config.toml; packs already written keep their dast checks as records

checkpoints.title: Never layer L07 (operational config): new config keys, and active_scan read only from the protected file. Why: an active scan attacks a running app, so who may turn it on is policy (Decision #485, G1), and the new defaults need a dated rollout (Decision #480). What changes: defaults.toml sets [verify] dast = true and new_floors_blocking_from = "2026-11-14", and [verify.floors.dast] skipped_blocks_ship = true; config.go adds Verify.NewFloorsBlockingFrom (validated as YYYY-MM-DD), Floors.DAST.SkippedBlocksShip, and Environment.ActiveScan; load.go refuses verify.environments.<env>.active_scan, in any letter case, from every layer except .aayudha/config.toml, and refuses an active_scan whose url another layer changed. This repository's .aayudha/config.toml sets [verify] platforms = ["cli", "web", "api"], so benefits-qa is scanned
contracts: internal/config/load.go: active_scan from the user, local, env, --set or config.json layer fails the load naming .aayudha/config.toml, a protected path
internal/config/load.go: an environment with active_scan = true must keep the url .aayudha/config.toml names
internal/config/config.go Validate: a malformed new_floors_blocking_from fails, so the new floors are never advisory forever
internal/config/schema.json and CONSTRAINTS.md regenerate from the structs and defaults.toml (internal/config/gen rows for the new keys)
instrumentation: aayu config show --origin names the layer each new key comes from
checkpoints.rollback: revert the PR, then remove any of the new keys a config file sets, because the loader refuses unknown keys (ErrorUnused); no ledger or stored state changes

checkpoints.title: Never layer L09 (platform): aayudha-security.yml runs the dast floor on every push to dev, rolling and main, and nightly. Why: Decision #485 puts DAST in the security floors, and this job is where the floors run outside a story. What changes: only the workflow's header comment; the job already runs `aayu verify --security`, which now includes dast. It never runs [verify] seed, because the job holds the token that writes aayudha:security Bugs and the seed is repository code; so it scans a deployed environment's url (AAYU_ENV) and shows a non-blocking `skipped: dast` for a loopback target or none. No permission, secret, trigger or pinned action changes. The init template (internal/initrepo/aayudha-security.yml) and its golden copy change the same way
contracts: .github/workflows/aayudha-security.yml: only the header comment changes; permissions, triggers, steps and action SHAs are unchanged; the dast result appears in the job summary that verify --security already writes
internal/initrepo/aayudha-security.yml is what `aayu init --gates` renders; internal/cli/testdata/gates/aayudha-security.yml is its golden copy
checkpoints.rollback: revert the PR; the workflow returns to sast, secrets and deps

checkpoints.title: CLI: `aayu verify --security` runs with NoSeed, and the waiver path releases a blocking dast skip; doctor shows the container runtime and the dast fix. LAYERS.md maps internal/doctor to no layer, so its rows are listed here, beside the verbs that print them
contracts: internal/cli/verifysecurity.go: the security run sets verify.Run.NoSeed
internal/cli verify: an accepted floor-waiver Decision naming dast releases `skipped: dast: no runnable target`
internal/doctor/security.go: a container-runtime row (docker, podman, or none) and the dast target row with the same fix verify prints
